# Close the last real grid column before unused width

## Context

Requested by @tobiu on 2026-09-19 from the cell-editing recording. A fixed-width grid has spare center space before its locked-end column; the last real center column has no visible right edge in either header or cells.

Reproduced in headed Chromium 153 at `c27c6648f5c56a39828490eda99627e70ca9bb91`, using the upper grid in `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing/index.html` at 1400×900. All six columns have explicit widths; none flexes.

## The Problem

`City` ends at x=631; locked-end `Note` begins at x=1239, leaving 608 px of intended unused width. City's cells have a 0 px right border. Its header has a 1 px **transparent** right border. The content block appears open into the gutter.

The gap is valid layout. Adding a flex column would change the consumer's declared widths and conceal the boundary defect.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/Row.mjs` adds `neo-last-column` to the last center/end column in a region.
- `resources/scss/src/grid/Body.scss` removes that class's right border; the first locked-end cell supplies its own left border.
- `resources/scss/src/grid/header/Button.scss` colors the right border only on `:not(:last-child)`.
- #9623 and the later seam-ownership reasoning addressed adjacent multi-body dividers. A border on Note's left edge does not close City's right edge when the two are 608 px apart.

## The Fix

Make the trailing edge of a real column visibly closed when it borders unused space. Keep the responsibility in the current row/header presentation and their geometry; use the existing logical column identity rather than pooled DOM-child order. Preserve the single-divider treatment when regions touch. The precise gap-header fill is a separate design question and need not block the missing-edge repair.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At the reproducer width, City's header and every rendered City cell have a visible, aligned right boundary at the real column edge.
- [ ] Resizing between spare-width and filled/overflowing layouts preserves alignment and avoids doubled dividers.
- [ ] Fixed-width grids with and without locked-end columns, plus an explicit flex-column control, retain their declared widths and normal separators.
- [ ] Horizontal pooling/scrolling and column lock changes retain correct boundary identity.
- [ ] Neo light/dark screenshots and geometry/style assertions cover both the exposed edge and contiguous-region control.

## Out of Scope

Adding automatic flex columns, changing width allocation, choosing the spare header area's fill, or altering focus/selection behavior.

Related: #9623, #9486, #18762 (observation context). Standalone visual follow-up.
